population-distribution-s1.title: Four places on a world map

map.label: Reference map of the world with four places marked: A in eastern China, B in the Sahara of North Africa, C in northern Canada and D in the Ganges River valley of India and Bangladesh

population-distribution-s2.title: People per square kilometer in the provinces of Country A

map.label: Choropleth map of Country A by province: people per square kilometer are highest in the Capital Region and along the South Coast and lowest in the Northern Hills and the Southern Forest

items.q: Look at the four lettered places on the map. Which two places are inside the world’s two largest clusters of people?
options: A and D
B and C
A and C
B and D

why.correct: Place A (eastern China) and Place D (the Ganges valley) sit in the East Asia and South Asia clusters, where more than half of the world’s people live.
options: Right: eastern China and the Ganges valley of South Asia are the two biggest clusters on Earth.
the Sahara and northern Canada are two of the emptiest places on Earth.
eastern China is crowded, but northern Canada has very few people.
the Ganges valley is crowded, but very few people live in the Sahara.

items.q: Very few people live at Place B. Which physical factor best explains this?
options: The land is too high and steep for farms, roads or most buildings
Very little rain falls, so there is little water for crops
Long, cold winters keep the ground frozen
Thick rainforest covers most of the land

why.correct: Place B is in the Sahara. With so little rain, there is not enough water to grow food, so few people live there.
options: that fits high mountains such as the Himalaya, not the Sahara at Place B.
Right: Place B is in the Sahara, one of the driest places on Earth.
that fits Place C in northern Canada, not the hot desert at Place B.
that fits the Amazon basin, not a desert.

items.q: Place B and Place C both have very few people. Which statement correctly compares the reasons?
options: Dryness limits where people live at both places
High mountains limit where people live at both places
Cold limits where people live at C, while dryness limits it at B
Heat limits where people live at Place C, while cold limits it at Place B

why.correct: Different physical factors can produce the same pattern: few people. Cold limits settlement in northern Canada, at Place C, and lack of water limits it in the Sahara, at Place B.
options: northern Canada is not mainly limited by dryness; its long, cold winters are the problem.
neither place is mainly a high mountain range.
Right: northern Canada is cold for most of the year, and the Sahara is very dry.
this swaps the two climates: C is cold and B is hot and dry.

items.q: At the global scale, Place A looks like one big cluster of people. What would a map of the same area at the local scale most likely show?
options: People spread evenly over the whole area, with no crowded or empty parts
Fewer people, because local maps leave out large parts of the area
Exactly the same picture as the world map, with no new detail
Crowded river plains and coast, with emptier hills between them

why.correct: The pattern you see depends on the scale of analysis. A world map shows eastern China as one cluster; a local map shows people packed onto river plains and the coast, with fewer in the hills.
options: local maps show more detail, and they reveal uneven patterns that the world map hides.
a local map covers less area but shows it in more detail; the people are still there.
changing the scale of analysis changes what you can see; a local map adds detail.
Right: a closer look shows the cluster has its own pattern: crowded lowlands, thinner hills.

items.q: At what scale of analysis are the data on this map?
options: Local (subnational): each province of Country A has its own value
National: the map shows the whole of Country A from border to border
Global: the map compares countries of the world
Regional: the map compares world regions

why.correct: The scale of analysis is the scale of the data shown, not the size of the area on the map. One value per province is local (subnational) data.
options: Right: the data are given for parts of one country, which is a subnational scale.
the map covers one country, but each value is for a province. The scale of analysis is the scale of the data.
there is only one country on this map.
a world region would hold several countries; these are provinces of one country.

items.q: Which statement best describes the pattern on the map?
options: People are spread fairly evenly across the eight provinces of Country A, with small differences
Highest in the Capital Region and South Coast, lowest in the Northern Hills and Southern Forest
The Northern Hills have the most people per square kilometer
People are clustered in the north and west of Country A

why.correct: A strong description of a pattern names where values are high and where they are low: the Capital Region (500 or more) and the South Coast (150 to 499) are highest; the Northern Hills and the Southern Forest (under 10) are lowest.
options: the provinces fall into five different classes, from under 10 to 500 or more.
Right: this names where the high and low values are, using the legend.
the Northern Hills are in the lowest class, under 10.
the north and west are in the two lowest classes.

items.q: The South Coast is crowded even though it is far from the capital. Which human factor best explains this?
options: Rain falls in most months of the year along the coast of Country A
The coast has flat land near the sea
A large port gives many people jobs in trade and shipping
The coast is the farthest province from the hills

why.correct: Human factors are things people create: jobs, transport, government and history. A port with jobs in trade is a human factor that draws people to the coast.
options: rain is a physical factor, and the question asks for a human one.
flat land is a physical factor, not a human one.
Right: jobs draw people, and a port links the coast to other countries.
distance from the hills does not by itself draw people.

items.q: Which question could this map NOT answer?
options: Which province has the most people per square kilometer
Whether the South Coast has more people per square kilometer than the Northern Hills
Which provinces are in the lowest class
Which towns inside the Northern Hills have the most people

why.correct: A province map gives one value for each province. It cannot show differences inside a province, such as which towns are crowded. That is a limit of the data at this scale.
options: the map shows this: the Capital Region is in the highest class.
the map shows this by comparing their classes.
the legend and shading show this.
Right: each province has one value, so the map hides differences inside a province.

items.q: Which term names the parts of Earth’s surface where people live permanently?
options: Ecumene
Population distribution
Situation
Formal region

why.correct: The ecumene is the part of Earth where people live permanently. Antarctica and the center of the Sahara lie outside it.
options: Right: the ecumene is the lived-in part of Earth.
population distribution is the pattern of where people live, not the lived-in area itself.
situation is a place’s location relative to other places.
a formal region shares a trait; it is not the lived-in part of Earth.

items.q: Most of Egypt’s people live in a narrow strip along the Nile River and in its delta. Which statement explains this pattern?
options: The river valley is the coldest part of Egypt
The river gives water for crops and drinking in a very dry country
The government moved people away from the coast and into the valley
The desert is too high and steep to build on

why.correct: Egypt is a desert country. The Nile gives water, so people have lived in its valley and delta for thousands of years. That is population distribution shaped by a physical factor.
options: temperature is not the reason; the rest of Egypt is a hot desert with almost no rain.
Right: water is the physical factor that draws people to the Nile.
Egypt’s pattern is old; it follows the water of the Nile.
most of Egypt’s desert is flat or rolling; it is the lack of water that matters.

items.q: Brazil built a new capital, Brasília, far inland in 1960 so that more people would live away from the coast. Which kind of factor shaping population distribution does this show?
options: A physical factor: a better climate inland
A physical factor: new rivers inland
A human factor: a government decision
Environmental determinism: the land forced people to move

why.correct: Governments shape where people live. Brasília is a human factor at the national scale: a political decision drew people and jobs inland.
options: the move was a government plan, not a change in climate.
no new rivers formed; the government chose the site.
Right: building a capital is a choice people make, so it is a human factor.
determinism says nature decides; here people decided.

items.q: A student writes, "Canada’s people are clustered." Which change makes this a strong description of the pattern?
options: Canada’s people are very clustered
Canada has a large area and a small population
Canada’s people are clustered because of its history, climate and economy
Most Canadians live in a band near the border with the United States

why.correct: Readers give no credit for "clustered" alone. A pattern needs a place: in Canada, most people live in a band near the southern border, and few live in the far north.
options: adding "very" still does not say where the people are.
this is true but says nothing about where people live inside Canada.
a reason does not replace the missing location of the cluster.
Right: this says where the cluster is, which is what a description needs.

items.q: Phoenix, in the desert of the southwestern United States, has more than a million people. Which idea best fits this case?
options: Possibilism: people adapt, for example by piping water to a dry place
Environmental determinism: the desert climate made the city grow large
Physical factors are the reason most people live in deserts
The ecumene does not include cities in dry places

why.correct: The desert limits settlement, but people brought in water and built air conditioning. That is possibilism: people adapt to an environment and choose how to use it.
options: Right: possibilism says the environment sets limits but people choose and adapt.
determinism says nature decides; deserts usually limit settlement.
most people do not live in deserts; dry climates usually limit settlement.
Phoenix is lived in permanently, so it is part of the ecumene.

items.q: Which of these are human factors that shape where people live? Select all that apply.
options: Jobs in factories and offices
Roads and railways
Rainfall
Mountains
Soil good for crops

why.correct: Human factors are made by people: jobs, transport, government decisions and history. Physical factors come from nature: climate, water, landforms and soil.
options: Right: jobs are created by people and draw them to a place.
Right: transport links are built by people and draw settlement along them.
Rainfall is a physical factor.
Mountains are a physical factor (a landform).
Soil is a physical factor.

items.q: Build an explanation of why few people live in a named place.

specific.frame: At the ___ scale, few people live in ___ because ___.
specific.model: At the national scale, few people live in Russia’s Siberia because its long, freezing winters make farming and building hard, so most Russians live in the west of the country.

scale.label: Scale of analysis
options: national
some

why.1: name a scale of analysis: local, national, regional or global.

place.label: Place
options: Russia’s Siberia
cold places

why.1: name a real place; "cold places" is too vague to earn credit.

cause.label: Cause and its link
options: its long, freezing winters make farming and building hard
it is cold

why.1: "it is cold" names a factor but does not say how it limits where people live.

why.correct: A strong answer names the scale, a real place and a cause with its link: cold winters, so farming and building are hard, so few people live there.

items.q: At the national scale, Australia looks almost empty. Which statement describes its population distribution at a more detailed scale?
options: Australians are spread fairly evenly across the interior and the coasts of the country
Most Australians live in the dry center of the country
Australia has no clusters of people
Most live in east and southeast coastal cities; the dry interior is nearly empty

why.correct: One national number hides a strong pattern. Most Australians live near the east and southeast coasts, where rain falls and the large cities are; the dry interior is nearly empty.
options: the dry interior has very few people.
the center is dry and has few people; the coasts are where most live.
Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane are large clusters on the coast.
Right: this names where people are and where they are not.

items.q: Many of the world’s large cities are on coasts or rivers. Which explanation links location to population distribution?
options: Coasts and rivers made trade and transport easier, so jobs and people gathered there
Coasts and rivers are cooler in summer, so people have long preferred to build homes there
People avoid inland places because most inland land is too steep to build on
Coasts have fewer people because ships take up space

why.correct: Physical and human factors work together. Water made moving goods cheaper, so trade, jobs and then people gathered on coasts and rivers.
options: Right: this links the physical setting to the human factor of trade.
temperature is not the reason, and the claim is not true.
much inland land is flat; trade is the reason.
the pattern is the opposite: many people live on coasts.

items.q: Order these places from most crowded to least crowded.
options: The Ganges River valley in northern India
The Great Plains of the central United States
Northern Siberia in Russia

why.correct: The Ganges valley is one of the most crowded farming regions on Earth; the Great Plains have farms and towns but far fewer people; northern Siberia has very few people because of the cold.
